commits.edited_message:
Reject invalid CENC IV metadata before decryption

Validate key records and per-sample IV sizes before configuring the decrypter. A constant IV may be any length the key-info record contains; the decrypter keeps the first 16 bytes. Check multikey SAI indices against the current declared key count so key-info changes cannot expose undeclared trailing records.

Keep the shared validator available without ISO media support and add regression coverage for valid and malformed IV metadata.

Fix PIFF default key-info size

The PIFF default-info getter reports 19 bytes for a 20-byte key
record. This truncates the advertised KID and causes CENC validation
to reject valid PIFF streams.

Return the key-info array's size. When the default IV is constant,
keep those bytes with the PIFF track encryption box. Add a regression
test that creates PIFF protection through the public API and checks
the returned size, record contents, and validation.

Verify valid PIFF playback, unchanged PIFF+CENC decryption output,
and all 13 existing CLI reproduction cases.

coupling: Commit 9fdc330 drops the constant-IV length cap in gf_cenc_validate_key_info (any length that is present in the key-info record is accepted) and only clamps the decrypter copies that existed in that commit, so a constant IV longer than 16 bytes is still safe there. Commit 35b6e6b then keeps a PIFF constant IV by copying key_info[20] bytes into a 16-byte buffer. That copy is within bounds only while the validator still rejects lengths other than 8 or 16; the PIFF commit does not repeat the cap because validation has already run. Neither edit overflows on its own: without the relaxed check the 32-byte constant IV is rejected before the copy, and without the PIFF retention the accepted record is only stored as the 16-byte KID. The overflow is the two together. Updating only the decrypter clamps leaves the PIFF copy in place; restoring only the 8-or-16 check, or sizing only that PIFF buffer from the validated length, each hide this input, but the two sites encode different contracts and a fix that touches just one of those diffs does not make the store and the validator agree.
